title: Where teen churchgoers are now, in their twenties
subtitle: Adults 23 to 30 who attended a Protestant church regularly for at least a year as teens
caption: Two thirds of this group dropped out for at least a year between ages 18 and 22, and 31 percent of those dropouts now attend twice a month or more. Today almost half attend at least twice a month; about one in five does not attend at all.
note: "Dropped out" is a church attendance measure, not a belief measure: it is the closest survey data to deconstruction, not deconstruction itself. "At least twice a month" includes the 27 percent who attend weekly or more.

sources.study: Most Teenagers Drop Out of Church When They Become Young Adults
sources.sample: 2,002 adults ages 23 to 30 who attended a Protestant church at least twice a month for at least a year in high school
